Of all the tickets printed for "LOTERIA®", only a small slice are still unsold. The game is close to selling out, with two of eight top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

If you play "LOTERIA®" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
959.headline: How much has sold

972.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "$8 Million Money Maker" are sold. The top prize count has held, with one of five still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

The second-biggest prize left on "$8 Million Money Maker" is $100,000, with one of them remaining.

The table below shows the full count for "$8 Million Money Maker", with every prize level included.
972.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

975.body:
The top prize count on "$1,000,000 Money Rush" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has two of four top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

The numbers for "$1,000,000 Money Rush" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
975.headline: Top prizes have lasted so far

976.body:
More than the top prize is gone on "100X The Cash". The top two prize levels have no prizes left. With the $2 million and $100,000 prizes all claimed, the biggest prize left is $10,000. The table on this page counts every prize below that.

Every line of 100X The Cash's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
976.headline: Top prize already claimed

980.body:
The most common win left on "20X The Cash" is $5. The second biggest prize left is $10,000, and four of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Today's free summary of "20X The Cash" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
980.headline: What's actually left to win

981.body:
"50X The Cash" is in the last part of its run, with only a small slice of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

If you play "50X The Cash" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
981.headline: How much has sold

985.body:
"MAX-A-MILLION" has gone three months without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About half of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $1 million prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

MAX-A-MILLION's prize setup is not better or worse than any other. Some games pay many small prizes and some pay a few large ones.

Every line of MAX-A-MILLION's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
985.headline: No top prize claimed lately

988.body:
The prize money on "Emerald 10's" leans toward many smaller prizes. It is spread over eleven prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $1 million. Games built like this pay small prizes often and large prizes rarely. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

Every line of Emerald 10's's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
988.headline: Same price, different prizes

990.body:
The most common win left on "LADY LUCK" is $2. The second biggest prize left is $1,000, and seven of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Today's free summary of "LADY LUCK" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
990.headline: A close look at the prizes

992.body:
"$2 MILLION VAULT" has had no $2 million top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

The table below shows the full count for "$2 MILLION VAULT", with every prize level included.
992.headline: No new top prize claims

993.body:
"$5,000 Triple Play" has gone five months without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About three-quarters of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $5,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

Tomorrow's count on "$5,000 Triple Play" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
993.headline: Top prizes have lasted so far

994.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "$25,000 Triple Play" have been sold. The game is past the halfway point of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

Every line of $25,000 Triple Play's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
994.headline: Early stage or late

995.body:
"$200,000 Triple Play" has two of four top prizes left and is well into its run. About two-thirds of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

If "$200,000 Triple Play" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
